identification.summary: REF7707 is Elastic Security Labs' name for an espionage-focused intrusion set first detailed publicly in February 2025, after Elastic saw endpoint alerts at a South American foreign ministry in late November 2024 [S1]. Its tooling includes FINALDRAFT, GUIDLOADER and PATHLOADER, and FINALDRAFT uses the Microsoft Graph API (Outlook drafts) for command and control [S1][S2]. Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 tracks overlapping activity as CL-STA-0049 and calls the backdoor Squidoor [S3]; Trend Micro tracks Earth Alux and notes REF7707 as another intrusion set using the same backdoor family (VARGEIT/FinalDraft) [S4][S9]; Symantec uses the name Jewelbug [S5]; Check Point uses Ink Dragon [S6].
identification.firstObserved: Elastic: first activity seen late November 2024 [S1]. Unit 42: active since at least March 2023 [S3]. Trend Micro (Earth Alux): first sighting Q2 2023 in APAC [S4].
identification.notes: Vendor cluster names are treated by several vendors as overlapping, not identical by Microsoft, which has no Typhoon/Sleet name for this actor in the sources gathered. Symantec states Jewelbug overlaps CL-STA-0049, Earth Alux and REF7707 [S5][S7]. Trend Micro describes REF7707 and Earth Alux as two intrusion sets that both use VARGEIT (FinalDraft in REF7707) [S9], which is narrower than a full merge. Trend Micro also describes SHADOW-EARTH-054 as having some network overlap with CL-STA-0049/REF7707 but a separate ShadowPad-based set [S9]. No Microsoft name identified.

attribution.sponsor: China-linked (vendor assessments); no government attribution found in the sources gathered. Specific state agency unconfirmed [S3][S7].
attribution.confidence: Unit 42 describes a 'suspected Chinese threat actor' [S3]. Reporting on the Check Point Ink Dragon report describes the China link as an assessment [S8]. Reporting on the August 2026 Symantec report is inconsistent: one summary says Symantec assessed with high confidence that the group works for China, most likely a state intelligence client with agency unconfirmed, while Dark Reading coverage says there is no direct evidence of a link to the PRC and the group could be acting for a state agency or on its own initiative [S7]. Treat as vendor-level, unresolved; verify against the Symantec primary text.
attribution.basis: Targeting pattern and tooling reported by Unit 42 and Symantec [S3][S7]; Symantec ties a commercial arm to a company registered in Hunan province, China [S7]; Trend Micro shares malware lineage with ShadowPad-using sets in the region [S9].

objectives: Espionage against government, defense, telecommunications, education and aviation targets, as described by Unit 42 [S3]. Symantec additionally reports a parallel for-profit cryptocurrency fraud operation run by the same team from a shared control panel [S7].

sectors: IT services (incl. a Russian IT service provider)
Technology, logistics, manufacturing, retail (Earth Alux reporting)
regions: Taiwan, Thailand, Malaysia, Philippines, Brazil (Earth Alux reporting)
targeting.notes: Elastic's first case was a South American foreign ministry; Southeast Asian telecom and university victims are reported by The Hacker News coverage and are single-sourced in my searches [S1][S2]. Unit 42 lists government, defense, telecom, education and aviation in Southeast Asia and South America [S3]. Trend Micro lists government, technology, logistics, manufacturing, telecom, IT services and retail across APAC and Latin America for Earth Alux [S4]. Symantec reports intrusion into a Russian IT service provider (January to May 2025) [S5]. Check Point reports several dozen victims across Europe, Asia and Africa, with growing focus on European government entities from mid-2025 [S8]. Symantec's 2026 report cites 15 government webmail tenants [S7].

capabilities.summary: Custom backdoors: FINALDRAFT (also Squidoor/VARGEIT in other vendors' naming), with Windows and Linux variants, using the Microsoft Graph API and Outlook drafts for C2 so traffic blends into legitimate Microsoft cloud traffic [S1][S2]. PATHLOADER runs first and decrypts fetched shellcode, which is FINALDRAFT injected into a new mspaint.exe process [S2]; GUIDLOADER is a second loader [S1]. The signed cdb.exe debugger is abused to run shellcode [S1][S3]. Unit 42 reports Squidoor supports Outlook API, DNS tunnelling and ICMP tunnelling for C2, with 10 C2 methods on Windows and nine on Linux [S3]. Initial access is typically exploitation of vulnerable IIS or other internet-facing servers followed by web shells (e.g. GODZILLA reported by Trend) [S3][S4]. Check Point reports ShadowPad use and compromised IIS servers turned into relay nodes with a custom listener module [S8]. In the Russian IT provider intrusion, Symantec reports credential dumping, scheduled-task persistence and exfiltration to Yandex Cloud [S5]. Elastic describes well-engineered tooling combined with poor operational security that exposed pre-production samples and additional infrastructure [S1].

campaigns.name: Earth Alux in APAC

campaigns.name: South American foreign ministry intrusion
campaigns.summary: Elastic sees a cluster of endpoint alerts at a South American foreign ministry and begins tracking REF7707, finding FINALDRAFT, GUIDLOADER and PATHLOADER.

campaigns.name: Public disclosure: Elastic and Unit 42
campaigns.summary: Elastic publishes REF7707 research (13 Feb) and the FINALDRAFT malware analysis; Unit 42 publishes Squidoor research on CL-STA-0049 (27 Feb per Malpedia-derived search summary).

campaigns.name: Trend Micro Earth Alux report
campaigns.summary: Trend Micro details Earth Alux toolkit (VARGEIT, COBEACON, GODZILLA, RAILLOAD, RAILSETTER).

campaigns.name: Russian IT service provider intrusion
campaigns.summary: Symantec reports Jewelbug in a Russian IT provider's build and code repository systems for about five months, exfiltrating to Yandex Cloud; reported October 2025.

campaigns.name: Check Point Ink Dragon report
campaigns.summary: Check Point reports several dozen victims across Europe, Asia and Africa, ShadowPad and FINALDRAFT use, and IIS relay nodes; European government focus since mid-2025.

campaigns.name: Trend Micro SHADOW-EARTH-053 report
campaigns.summary: Trend Micro describes a separate set (SHADOW-EARTH-054) with some network overlaps to CL-STA-0049/REF7707.

campaigns.name: Symantec espionage and crypto fraud report
campaigns.summary: Symantec reports the team runs espionage and crypto fraud from one control panel (XG-Web), including compromised webmail of 15 government tenants.

diamond.adversary: China-linked espionage actor tracked under several vendor names; sponsor agency unconfirmed [S3][S7].
diamond.capability: FINALDRAFT/Squidoor/VARGEIT backdoors, PATHLOADER and GUIDLOADER, cdb.exe abuse, web shells, ShadowPad [S1][S3][S8].
diamond.infrastructure: Microsoft Graph/Outlook and other legitimate cloud services for C2, Yandex Cloud for exfiltration, compromised IIS servers as relays [S1][S5][S8].
diamond.victim: Governments, defense, telecom, education, aviation and IT service providers across South America, Asia, Europe, Africa, Middle East and Russia [S3][S5][S8].
diamond.socioPolitical: Government and ministry targeting is consistent with intelligence collection; Symantec also reports financially motivated fraud by the same team [S3][S7].
diamond.technology: Internet-facing IIS servers, webmail and shared hosting platforms, Microsoft 365 / Outlook cloud APIs, and software build environments [S3][S5][S7].

gaps: Elastic, Unit 42, Symantec and Check Point primary pages could not be fetched (host unreachable); content is taken from search-result summaries and secondary coverage. Verify details against primaries.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain includes internet-facing IIS servers, webmail and shared hosting platforms, Microsoft 365/Outlook tenants, and IT service provider build systems that sit upstream of government clients [S3][S5][S7]. STEP 2: The actor blends C2 into Microsoft Graph and cloud storage traffic, and compromised servers act as relays, which complicates attribution of traffic [S1][S8]. STEP 3: Template is web-server exploitation, web shell, cdb.exe-launched loader, FINALDRAFT/Squidoor with cloud C2, credential dumping, scheduled-task persistence, cloud exfiltration [S1][S3][S5]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued espionage against government, defense, telecom and aviation entities in the regions reported [S3][S8]. MDCOA is a supply-chain pivot through an IT service provider's build or code systems to downstream government clients, as the Russian case shows was reachable [S5]. Candidate indicators: cdb.exe executing scripts or shellcode, mspaint.exe hosting injected code, unexpected Graph API or Outlook draft activity from servers, new ASPX files on IIS (e.g. OutlookDC.aspx), and DNS or ICMP tunnelling [S2][S3].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track vendor cluster names together (REF7707, CL-STA-0049, Earth Alux, Jewelbug, Ink Dragon) so reporting is not fragmented [S5][S6]. (2) Authorities: no government attribution exists in the sources, so response should rest on technical indicators, not named-actor authority. (3) Mission assurance: harden and monitor internet-facing IIS and webmail, and review cloud-API egress from servers, particularly for contractor and partner-nation systems [S3][S8]. (4) Coordination: share indicators with allied and partner governments, since victims span South America, Asia, Europe and Africa, and with IT service providers that hold build environments [S5][S8].
